dedupe_keys.name: fixmystreet uk street problem reports and open source reporting platform

description: FixMyStreet, created by mySociety in 2007, lets people report street problems such as potholes and broken street lights to the UK council responsible, by placing a pin on a map; the site works out the authority and sends the report by email or through Open311. Reports are public, so others can see and update them or subscribe to local alerts. On 26 September 2026 the dashboard showed 8,009,515 problems reported and 3,135,705 marked fixed, with 24,953 new reports in the previous seven days. The FixMyStreet Platform, now version 6.0, is open-source software reused by others, for example Züri wie neu in Zurich and Fixa min gata in Sweden. Coverage: councils across the UK, including parish councils. Access: public report pages and a read-only Open311 search API returning up to 1,000 requests per query. Licence: site conditions of use for the data. Caveats: the API is labelled work in progress and may change without warning, and reporting reflects who chooses to report. Simulation uses: condition and defect signals for streets, lighting and public realm assets. Related records: NYC 311 requests and the Open311 standard.
